Rashi on Pesachim 113a:10:1.english: Go out last - For if you flee, you will enter your house first.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:11:1.hebrew: אל תרבה בגנות - כלומר, אל תהא רגיל לעשות בית בפרהסיא, במקום מגולה:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:11:1.english: Do not frequent gardens - That is to say, do not be accustomed to making a house in public, in an exposed place.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:11:2.english: Because of the incident that occurred - With David and Bathsheba.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:11:3.english: Due to money - For she squanders your money on him.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:1:1.hebrew: גזייתא - כשמהלכים במבואות שבילי כרמים, וסוסיהן משתמטין מכאן ובורחין ביישוב, אתו ודברי להו:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:1:1.english: Gazyata - When [the demons] travel in the lanes, [that is,] vineyard paths, and their horses slip away from there and flee into the inhabited area, they come and lead them [back].

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:1:2.hebrew: שראשה אסיא - רופא, ואמרי לה ת"ח, ותרוייהו חד טעמא:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:1:2.english: [A city] whose head is an asya - A physician, and some say a Torah scholar, and both [have] one reason.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:1:3.english: Horses - Because it is a protection in the city from enemies and from thieves.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:2:1.hebrew: ולא תינסב תרי - נשים, שמא תתיעצנה עליך רעה:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:2:1.english: And do not marry two - women, lest they conspire evil against you.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:2:2.hebrew: נסיב תלת - שאם תתיעצנה, השלישית מגלה לך:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:2:2.english: Marry three - For if they conspire [against you], the third reveals [it] to you.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:3:1.english: Skin a carcass - Flay its hide.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:3:2.hebrew: סלקת לאיגרא שירותך בהדך - כשתצא לדרך אפי' קרובה, צא ומזונותיך עמך:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:3:2.english: [If] you go up to the roof, [take] your meal with you - When you set out on a journey, even a short [one], go out with your food with you.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:3:3.hebrew: מאה קרי בזוזי תותי כנפיך להוו - אפילו המזונות בזול, אעפ"כ הוציאם עמך:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:3:3.english: A hundred pumpkins for zuzim, let them be under the corners [of your garment] - Even [if] food is cheap, nevertheless, take them out with you.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:4:1.hebrew: לא תשתי סמא - לא תלמד לשתות סמים, מפני שתקבע להון ווסת ויהא לבך שואלך ותפזר מעות. ל"א: לא תהא רגיל לשתות סממנים, כדאמר (לעיל פסחים מב:): (כולהו שקייני) דמעלי להאי, קשה להאי:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:4:1.english: Do not drink a potion - Do not train yourself to drink potions, because you will establish a regular habit for them, and your heart will crave [them], and you will squander money. Another explanation: Do not be accustomed to drink medications, as it says (above, Pesachim 42b): (all potions,) that which is beneficial for this [organ is] harmful for that [one].

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:4:2.english: Do not leap over a ditch - [This involves] a wide stride, which diminishes [one's] eyesight.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:4:3.hebrew: ולא תעקר ככא - שן ממש, משום חולי:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:4:3.english: And do not pull out a tooth - Literally a tooth, on account of illness.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:5:1.hebrew: דמלכותייהו אחורי אודנייהו קיימי - כלומר, עתידין לגדל ותגדל אימתן, וינקמו ממך:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:5:1.english: Because their authority stands behind their ears - That is to say, they are destined to grow up, and the dread of them will grow, and they will take vengeance on you.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:6:1.hebrew: אדחלא על כרעך זבינך זבין - בעוד שהחול על רגליך כשבאת מן הדרך, מכור מה שהבאת כדי שתחזור ותקנה ותביא:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:6:1.english: While the sand is on your feet, sell your merchandise - While the sand is on your feet when you have come from the road, sell what you have brought so that you may go back and buy and bring [more].

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:7:1.hebrew: שרי כיסך ופתח שקך - כלומר, תקבל תחלה המעות ותנם בכיסך, ואח"כ פתח השק ותן התבואה ללוקחים:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:7:1.english: Open your purse and open your sack - That is to say, first receive the money and place it in your purse, and afterward open the sack and give the grain to the buyers.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:7:2.hebrew: קבא מארעא ולא כורא מאיגרא - כלומר, טוב לילך למקום קרוב ולהשתכר מעט, מלהשתכר הרבה במדינת הים:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:7:2.english: A kav from the ground and not a kor from the roof - That is to say, [it is] better to go to a nearby place and earn a little than to earn much overseas.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:8:1.hebrew: תמרי בחלוזך לבי סודנא רהוט - אם יש לך תמרים באותו כלי שנותנים בו תמרים, רוץ מיד לבית עושה שכר לעשות מהן שכר, שאם תמתין, תאכלם בין כך ובין כך ותפסיד:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:8:1.english: Dates in your chaluz, run to the brewery - If you have dates in that vessel in which they put dates, run immediately to the house of a beer-maker to make beer from them, for if you wait, you will eat them in the meantime and lose [out].

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:8:2.english: What is sudana - Why is the beer called sudana?

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:8:3.hebrew: סוד נאה - עצה טובה, שהרי מתעשרין הימנה:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:8:3.english: A pleasant secret - Good counsel, for indeed [people] become wealthy from it.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:8:4.english: And acts of loving-kindness - [One] is able to give a gift to the poor and to perform charity and kindness.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:9:1.hebrew: כל אגב גביא בעיא - כל דבר שצריך לכתוב שטר עליו, כגון מלוה ואמנה, בעייא גביא; כלומר, עדיין עומד הוא לגבות, ויש לו טורח בו:
Rashi on Pesachim 113a:9:1.english: Every [transaction] by means of [a document] requires collection - Anything for which one needs to write a document, such as a loan and [a sale on] credit, requires collection; that is to say, it still stands to be collected, and he has trouble with it.

Rashi on Pesachim 113a:9:2.english: Bad money - For [the buyer] pays them to them a zuz at a time.

Tosafot on Pesachim 113a:10:1.hebrew: עשה שבתך חול ואל תצטרך לבריות - והא דאמרינן בפ"ב דביצה (דף טז:) דבהוצאת שבתות וימים טובים, אם פוחת פוחתין לו — היינו בשלו, אם יש לו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 113a:10:1.english: Make your Shabbat [like] a weekday and do not be beholden to [other] people - And that which we say in the second chapter of Beitzah (16b), that regarding expenditures for Shabbatot and festivals, if he reduces [his spending], they reduce [his allotment] for him — that is [when spending] from his own [means], if he has [any].

Tosafot on Pesachim 113a:12:1.hebrew: דמשייר מקדושא לאבדלתא - שמונע שתייתו בשביל הבדלה. ותימה, דהא דוקא קידוש לילה קודם לכיבוד יום, אבל הבדלה אינה קודמת. ומפרש מורי הר"י דקידוש יום קרי כיבוד יום; והכי איתא בירושלמי פרק שלשה שאכלו: רבי יוסי בשם רבי יעקב ב"ר אדא: איזהו כיבוד יום? בפה"ג:
Tosafot on Pesachim 113a:12:1.english: Who leaves some of [his] kiddush [wine] for havdalah - [Meaning] that he refrains from drinking it for the sake of havdalah. And this is puzzling, for only the nighttime kiddush takes precedence over honoring the day, whereas havdalah does not take precedence. And my teacher, R"I [Rabbi Yitzchak], explains that it calls daytime kiddush "honoring the day"; and so it is stated in the Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Sheloshah She'achlu: "Rabbi Yose [said] in the name of Rabbi Yaakov bar Rabbi Ada: What is honoring the day? With [the blessing over] the fruit of the vine."

Tosafot on Pesachim 113a:3:1.english: And do not say: I am a priest - I explained [this] in [the chapter entitled] Eilu Ovrin (above, Pesachim 49b):

Tosafot on Pesachim 113a:8:1.hebrew: אמר רב פפא אי לאו דרמאי שיכרא לא איעתרי - ובשילהי אלו עוברין (שם) קאמר רב פפא: "אי לאו דנסיבי כהנתא לא איעתרי". י"ל דהא והא גרמא ליה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 113a:8:1.english: Rav Pappa said: If I had not brewed beer, I would not have become wealthy - And at the end of [the chapter] Eilu Ovrin (there), Rav Pappa says: "If I had not married a kohenet, I would not have become wealthy." One can say that both this and that caused it for him.
